_phase.name: Maintenance — recovering expenditure
_phase.why: Not a deficit. MacroFactor measured expenditure falling from 2462 in March to 1801 now — 767 kcal, of which only ~270 is explained by lost mass and fewer steps. At 1600 the deficit had shrunk to ~200 kcal and was still closing; cutting further would have pushed expenditure down again. Eating at measured expenditure is what lets it climb back, and a deficit from a recovered 2100 loses fat faster than one from 1800.
_phase.expect: 1-1.5 kg on the scale in week one. That is water and glycogen refilling, not fat — 300 kcal a day cannot become a kilo of fat in a week. Do not react to it. Judge this phase on the MacroFactor expenditure line, not on bodyweight.
_phase.alsoRequired: Steps back to 8000/day. That is ~200 kcal of real expenditure and it is what actually moved the weight in July. The calorie change alone does half the job.
_phase.thenWhat: Re-import MacroFactor on 2026-09-26 and run check_targets.py. If expenditure has climbed above ~2000, drop to expenditure minus 400 for the next cut. If it has not moved at all, the logging is the suspect, not the metabolism.

_phase.name: Provisional — modelled, not measured
_phase.why: Her four targets come from an activity-factor model and nothing else. The same model said Philipp's maintenance was 2424-2688 kcal; MacroFactor measured 1801. A model that was 600 kcal wrong about one person in this household is not evidence about the other. 1580 is a starting guess with roughly +-300 kcal in it, and it should be treated as one until there is an expenditure line to check it against.
_phase.theOpenQuestion: Whether 45 g of protein fits outside lunch and dinner in practice. On paper it is 250 g of skyr and a scoop of whey; in a real morning it is a habit she does not have yet.
_phase.expect: Two weeks of hitting 3 of 4 targets on most days. Not perfection — the question is whether the shape of the day is livable, not whether the arithmetic closes.
_phase.thenWhat: If the protein lands: keep 125 and start trusting the number. If breakfast keeps coming up short, fall back to protein 120 / fat 47 / net carbs 153 — already worked out, same 1580 kcal, and it costs 0.08 g/kg. Do not fall back by eating less protein while leaving the target at 125; change the target, so the report keeps telling the truth.
_phase.blocking: She has no MacroFactor data at all — private/macrofactor holds only philipp. Until she logs, this phase can only be reviewed against the scale and how she feels, which is exactly the weak evidence that produced the 600 kcal error. Two weeks of logging before 2026-09-26 would give the first real read.

mirrorMeals.note: Lunch and dinner are identical in size and macros for both people. Fat is a CEILING, not a range: protein and fibre are hit first and fat lands where it lands underneath it. A floor of 8 g was doing nothing — a leaner dish simply leaves the snack more room — while the 12 g ceiling put salmon, eggs, tempeh and tofu out of reach of a 40 g protein meal. Written as "0-14" so every reader that splits the range keeps working; read it as "up to 14".
mirrorMeals._revised: 2026-08-29 — was 425 kcal / 17 g fibre / 12-15 g fat on 1.5 Asian Base blocks. That target could not be cooked: the cheapest combination of these staples reaching it came to 533 kcal, 108 kcal over, at every meal. Raised to 470 kcal on 1 block with 14 g fibre, which the same search reaches at 432 kcal — leaving real slack for sauce and aromatics instead of sitting on the theoretical floor. Run scripts/check_targets.py after touching any of these numbers.
mirrorMeals._revised2: 2026-08-30 — fat band 8-12 -> ceiling of 14, no floor. The day pays for it out of slack it already had: Philipp keeps 17 g of fat for the snack, Eunice 24 g for breakfast plus snack. check_targets.py's REAL FOOD search goes from 4962 to 5697 plates on one block and returns tofu at every block level, salmon on the saucy tier.
mirrorMeals._revised3: 2026-08-30 — mirror meal 470 -> 520 kcal, and Eunice's protein 105 -> 125 g with fat 52 -> 45 and net carbs 160 -> 151 paying for it. Her breakfast-plus-snack envelope was 640 kcal asking for 25 g of protein: 40% of her day, 16% of it accounted for. Because lunch and dinner are identical for both people, growing the meal shrinks both envelopes at once — hers to 540, his to 450. Protein per meal stays 40: raising it would have relieved his snack and emptied hers, which is backwards. The ceiling on how far this can go is HIS snack, which reaches 32% protein at 520 and 37% at 550. Cooking gets easier, not harder — check_targets.py finds 18260 plates at 520 against 11992 at 470.

_gaps: Five dishes were rebuilt on 2026-08-30 (legume as the fibre carrier, fat cut, meat cut, solve() re-fits). Two of the five were reverted the same day: edamame is Japanese, and putting it in a Vietnamese phở and a Korean stew was a macro fix in costume — it also cost the brisket that IS phở bò chín and the potatoes that thicken a dakbokkeumtang. Root cause was in the data: topUps filed edamame under 'asian', which is a continent rather than a cuisine. Fixed there too.

Two dishes are marked fibreLight and are meant to be: pho-bo (4.8 g) and korean-spicy-chicken-stew (6.1 g). Both close the day beside any of the four 14 g dishes plus 7-9 g of psyllium, inside the 10 g cap. The phở gained its fibre honestly rather than by redesign — the transcription had 40 g of sprouts and no herbs, which is not how phở is served. The rau sống plate (200 g sprouts, Thai basil, coriander, mint, lime) is canonical and carries 4.5 g a serving. That was a missing half of the dish, not a macro patch.

Eunice's four targets imply 1598 kcal against a 1580 budget — an 18 kcal rounding gap, left alone. Her numbers have no MacroFactor data behind them, so the model is all there is, and the model was 600 kcal wrong for Philipp. Believe her scale over this arithmetic.

The Vorratsdose has never been tasted, only calculated. It is built against acidity rather than macros — skyr instead of quark, cocoa in the bowl, banana instead of the tart frozen berries, almond milk to loosen it, salt to blunt the sourness. If skyr is still too sour the next step is Greek yoghurt 0-2%, NOT more sweetener: sweetness masks acid, fat and salt remove it. Mix a small test batch before committing 1.5 kg.

baked-feta-salmon-light lands at 22.2 g of fat against a 14 g per-meal guideline, and that is arithmetic rather than a recipe fault: salmon carries 0.67 g of fat per gram of protein, so 40 g of protein from salmon alone is 26.8 g of fat before anything else. Prawns carry part of the protein and the feta is down from 200 g to 80, which halves the fat from 43. It closes the day next to a lean dish (lemon-herb-chicken-light) and not twice in one day — which is exactly why the planner checks pairs.
_bodyNote: Body composition is NOT in this file and must never be. It lives in private/body.json, which is gitignored, because this repo is public and a bodyweight describes a person rather than a plan. scripts/check_targets.py reads it from there and degrades to a warning when it is absent.

_dayShape.summary: Two blocks outside the mirror meals. Morning is per-person and NOT shared; the afternoon pudding IS shared. Sharing only pays off where there is a batch operation — the same reason lunch and dinner are identical. The morning is portioned per person anyway, so unifying it would be cosmetic and would cost Eunice a habit that works.

morning.philipp: philipp-overnight-oats — mixed the night before, eaten around 10 at school. philipp-whey-shaker stays in the library for days when no jar travels.
morning.eunice: eunice-ehrmann-pudding-breakfast — bought, sealed, unchanged. She declined overnight oats because she will not pack a second jar for work; that objection is hers and does not generalise to him.

afternoon.sweet: die-vorratsdose-skyr-schoko-nuss — ONE bowl, 9 portions, 3 days. Philipp 2 a day, Eunice 1, ~155 g a portion. Skyr for both; nut butter and cocoa mixed in, banana per portion.
afternoon.savoury_meat: die-herzhafte-dose-linsen-pute-paprika — 4 portions. Turkey poached, not roasted. Sesame oil and lemon go on at the bowl, never into the batch.
afternoon.savoury_quark: kraeuterquark-mit-linsen — 4 portions. Kräuterquark was ruled out because Eunice does not eat Magerquark, but that objection belonged to the SWEET context: the same tang reads wrong in a sweet bowl and right in a herb dip. No lemon, no vinegar.
afternoon._swapping: All three sit at 275-277 kcal, so any mix closes both days on all four macros without recalculating. Verified across every combination.
afternoon._fatCorrection: 2026-08-30: all three were built fat-phobic by reflex, and the aroma in all of them is fat-soluble — herbs, cocoa, cinnamon. Fat went in as a TRADE, not an addition: the calorie window was already full even though the fat column was not, and fat costs 9 kcal a gram. Sweet bowl: 54 g nut butter in, banana halved, oat bran 171 to 140. Quark bowl: 16 g olive oil in, quark 800 to 660. The turkey bowl needed no fat at 4.7 g and got only technique fixes.

_dayShape.batchRhythm: The pudding is mixed twice a week, not once for three days: 3 portions a day makes a 3-day batch ~2.1 kg in one tub. It needs no heat and no cooling, so twice is the same total work with fresher berries. The 3-day rhythm stays for lunch and dinner, where it exists because of the cooking.
_dayShape.fibreTiming: Fibre does not have to be eaten in the morning — only the daily total matters for what fibre is for. What is true is the satiety argument: fibre slows gastric emptying, so a morning item without it holds less long. That is why the shaker suits someone who does not want to eat in the morning anyway.

topUp._why: A six-day simulation showed both eating short every day: Philipp 95-116 kcal, Eunice 195-216 — 13% of her day. Mechanical, not behavioural: the light dishes come in at 450 and 487 kcal against a 520 spec, twice a day.
topUp.calories: ehrmann-pudding-nachfueller — a cup from the fridge. Nothing to mix, nothing to remember, already on the shopping list. Brings Eunice to -21 kcal; Philipp only needs one on some days (a whole one puts him +58 to +79 over, which is noise but not nothing).
topUp.fibre: A capped spoon of Flohsamenschalen, see kitchen.json dayFineTuning. Over the same six days the largest gap was 8 g of powder against a 10 g cap, and on the days with the light dishes none was needed at all.
topUp._deleted: There was briefly a third recipe here — a Nachfüller of skyr, berries and oat bran. Deleted. It closed the same hole as a bought cup while being one more thing to mix and remember, and this household does not need a third decision at the end of a stressed day. Fewer moving parts beats a slightly better fit.
